Sentence (English): I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much.
Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Sentence (English): So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes.
Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Sentence (English): Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall.
Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!
