Sentence (English): Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!
Comments (English): Among the 14-person LG dishwashers, this is the model with a 10cm mop holder, so I bought this. Until 4 years ago, I used an S Magic 6-person dishwasher that was placed on top of the sink when I was a family of 3, but the space was too narrow to put the dishes and pots and pans that were used after cooking for the family at dinner in the 6-person dishwasher. So I washed the large pots separately by hand and only put the dishes in the dishwasher. Later, it was difficult to play Tetris in the cramped 6-person dishwasher, so I washed all the dishes by hand and the dishwasher was relegated to just being used as a dish rack after washing the dishes. Then I got rid of it and stopped using the dishwasher and just washed the dishes by hand. This year, my second child was born, and I was busy taking care of my newborn second child and taking my first child, who is in first grade, to school and pick-up from school. I didn't have time or energy to wash the dishes, and my wrists hurt too much. My husband tells me not to wash the dishes during the day and to save them since he will do the dishes after dinner, but if I save everything from breakfast, baby food, dinner, etc., they really pile up in the sink, but I can't stand seeing them pile up, so I have to do them right away. So even though I'm busy, I make time to wash the dishes. I wash my hands and use detergent so many times a day to take care of the baby, and now I have housewife's eczema and an unknown skin disease on the back of my hands. If I wear rubber gloves, it gets worse because of the moisture. My caring husband always volunteers to do the dishes without complaint, but since he's tied up in the kitchen for almost an hour to do the dishes, I have to take care of the kids. I have to help my first grader with his homework and take care of my second newborn. Dinner time flies by in a flash, and it's the golden time of the day when the whole family gathers, but the time that all four of us can spend together is reduced due to washing dishes, so I thought I absolutely had to get a dishwasher, so I started looking into dishwashers around fall. I compared LG's and Sam's with similar specs and a 10cm mop holder, and the big features are that Sam's has a water filter and it's not made in Korea, LG's has the advantage of a True Steam function, and unlike Sam's, you have to add salt and it's made in Korea. 10 years ago, when I got married, I learned that white goods should definitely be LG, so I bought all of the wedding appliances from LG, but the TV, washing machine, and refrigerator all had defects so I had to get after-sales service. 4 years ago, when I moved into my current home, I installed an LG system air conditioner as an option when it was sold (not a custom-made one), but due to a defective drain pump, water leaked, and one night while I was sleeping, water leaking from the system air conditioner attached to the ceiling hit my head. 2 years ago, although I really didn't want to pay for another LG product, I bought an 86-inch LG TV based on the common sense(?) that I should definitely buy an LG TV. This summer, 2 years later, the motherboard suddenly malfunctioned, and I had to pay over 200,000 won for repairs and after-sales service. To that extent, my family has had more than one or two headaches with LG appliances, to the point that we're currently replacing all of our appliances with new ones. I was worried that it would break down again when I brought in an LG dishwasher. Nevertheless, I chose the LG dishwasher because it's manufactured in Korea. We can use the Sam* employee mall, and since we are related to Sam* employees, we could have bought a Sam* dishwasher with the same specs as this model for about 300,000 won cheaper, but we decided on this LG model because we thought better is better. After deciding to purchase this model, we watched the price trend starting in the fall, and the price on Coupang fluctuated significantly within a day or two. After watching, we bought it on the day the price suddenly dropped. An LG technician came and did the delivery/installation. Since the sink in my house is a 600-size standard, we could just separate the storage cabinets, but we had to cut out the mop holder and reinforce the inner support, so we spent an additional 80,000 won in labor costs. Since I had used a 6-person dishwasher until a few years ago, I know everything about dish Tetris and larval washing, so I have no inconveniences in using it. The Tetris of the dishes is something you get used to using it, and for the pre-washing, after you finish eating, collect the food, wash it with water, and then soak it in a large bowl filled with water. This way, you can remove some of the food without having to use a scrubber. It is definitely much wider than the 6-person dishwasher I used before, so there is no stress about Tetris of putting dishes in the narrow dishwasher. Because the space is wide, you can just put them in. The exterior size is the same as the old 12-person model with 2 baskets, but this 14-person model has 3 baskets, so there is more storage for dishes. The downside is that it is more comfortable than washing dishes by hand, but the electricity bill is high, and you have to bend down to put the dishes in. However, if you use it, your quality of life will change, so I recommend it to those who are considering buying it. Buy it as soon as possible and be free from washing dishes!

Sentence (English): I hesitated because there were really no reviews of products I bought with my own money, but I wanted to use it, but there is a limit, so I gave it a try and I am very satisfied, so I am leaving a review.
Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were really no reviews of products I bought with my own money, but I wanted to use it, but there is a limit, so I gave it a try and I am very satisfied, so I am leaving a review. First of all, the situation of my house. - 25 pyeong lease, difficulty with built-in. - Not suitable for Samsung, LG 6-person installation due to the unique structure of the kitchen. (There is a hole drilled, but it cannot be installed in a location where the drain line passes through the induction, it cannot be installed because it cannot be placed within 30cm of the induction (burner), the size is not suitable to be placed right next to the sink, etc.) I bought the product because I was told that it can be installed without drilling and next to the induction or burner. The next day, the technician contacted me to coordinate the installation time, and it was installed the day after I purchased it. The technician initially seemed uneasy about our small and unique kitchen layout, but he kindly helped me figure it out, which is another area where I'm very satisfied. With the upcoming baby and the burden of dishwashing, I reluctantly decided to buy a six-person unit, but I'm more than satisfied. The setup is incredibly simple and perfect for cooking breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My poor stacking skills may have played a role, but after using it for about three weeks, I find myself using a frying pan for every meal, whether it's meat or fries, and occasionally using a pot. If I add a frying pan and a pot, I think I can only cook for one meal. When I run it once a day, I run it except for the wooden utensils, frying pan, and pot. When I add the pot and pan, I run it for one meal. The button operation is also very simple. Just turn it on (there's a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything cleanly. It even cleans the frying pan I used to cook LA ribs in, and the plate I used to cook the red grease leftover from the spicy stir-fry. Additionally, it can rinse and wash, but I haven't used it yet. The UV sterilization mode and door-opening function can be turned on and off, and I think it would be convenient for the elderly, so I seriously want to buy one for my mom's house. However, if there are more than three people, the 6-person size is small, so I recommend the 12-14-person size. I recommend it for families with 1-2 people + a baby, homes without built-in appliances, or homes without other facilities. High-heat drying? There's no separate drying function, so I was a little confused at first. Just soaking it in water once cleans the inside and outside of the dishwasher, even the grease, and it's clean. However, water does accumulate in the concave area on the back of the bowl where it spilled. However, the door opens automatically, and when I turn it on after dinner, there are only a few drops of moisture left in the concave area the next morning. We don't even like that, so we just leave it in the sink to dry completely when it's done. It's not inconvenient at all, and I actually enjoy the feeling of freshly washed dishes! For your information, my house is not able to take full advantage of the L-shape, and it only opens about 45 degrees because of the faucet part, but I am satisfied with it and using it. Stack the first layer first and then assemble the second layer to fill it. It may look inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are satisfactory, so if there is anyone who needs it in a special structure like ours, I recommend it for purchase. If you have a larger kitchen, I recommend it because it will be much easier to use when it fully unfolds into an L-shape. The setup is incredibly simple and perfect for cooking breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My poor stacking skills may have played a role, but after using it for about three weeks, I find myself using a frying pan for every meal, whether it's meat or fries, and occasionally using a pot. If I add a frying pan and a pot, I think I can only cook for one meal. When I run it once a day, I run it except for the wooden utensils, frying pan, and pot. When I add the pot and pan, I run it for one meal. The button operation is also very simple. Just turn it on (there's a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything cleanly. It even cleans the frying pan I used to cook LA ribs in, and the plate I used to cook the red grease leftover from the spicy stir-fry. Additionally, it can rinse and wash, but I haven't used it yet. The UV sterilization mode and door-opening function can be turned on and off, and I think it would be convenient for the elderly, so I seriously want to buy one for my mom's house. However, if there are more than three people, the 6-person size is small, so I recommend the 12-14-person size. I recommend it for families with 1-2 people + a baby, homes without built-in appliances, or homes without other facilities. High-heat drying? There's no separate drying function, so I was a little confused at first. Just soaking it in water once cleans the inside and outside of the dishwasher, even the grease, and it's clean. However, the door opens automatically, and when I turn it on after dinner, there are only a few drops of moisture left in the concave area the next morning. If you have a larger kitchen, I recommend it because it will be much easier to use when it fully unfolds into an L-shape. For your information, our kitchen is right next to the sink, so we did not drill a separate hole, but connected the drain pipe directly to the sink, and installed the part where the water is drawn along the wall next to it, so we are satisfied with the appearance. Since Coupang also provides after-sales service, I plan to use it conveniently. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with the price-to-quality ratio!

Sentence (English): We purchased this on Saturday after our dishwasher by another brand died.
Comments (English): [ Love the quietness ] || ---------------- || We purchased this on Saturday after our dishwasher by another brand died. We recently refurbished our kitchen so our other appliances are now all black. This Whirlpool Maxi tub model was available in black, was in-stock and was on sale. Woohoo! My husband was able to install it himself although the installation instructions are very basic and could do with better details. So far it's doing a great job of cleaning the dishes. It is also really quiet compared to our last dishwasher so we're really happy about that! We live in an area that has hard water so we were also pleased that this dishwasher has a water softener section that you fill with dishwasher salt to soften the water. This sounded great in theory until we found out none of the local supermarkets or hardware stores stock it. It fact they haven't even heard of dishwasher salt and acted very sceptically towards us! I think that Whirlpool need to promote the use of the dishwasher salts and ensure supplies in local areas if they are going to manufacture and sell models with this option. Other features include a cutlery shelf which cleans cutlery better than a basket. I also like the option of a half-load. All in all a good dishwasher for a great price.

Sentence (English): I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money.
Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Sentence (English): I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner.
Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Sentence (English): With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected.
Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Sentence (English): The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean.
Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!

Comments (English): [ This is a review of a product I bought with my own money. ] || ---------------- || I hesitated because there were hardly any reviews from people who bought this with their own money. However, I desperately wanted to use it but felt I had my limits, so I decided to take the plunge. I am very satisfied, so I am leaving this review. First, let me explain my home situation: - We are renting a 25-pyeong apartment, which makes built-in appliances difficult. - Due to the unique structure of our kitchen, Samsung and LG 6-person models were unsuitable for installation. (For reasons such as drainage lines passing through the induction cooktop even though there were pre-drilled holes, the cooktop could not be placed within 30cm of the burner, and the size was unsuitable for placing right next to the sink.) I purchased this product because it claimed to be drill-free and could be installed next to an induction cooktop or burner. The technician contacted me the very next day to schedule the installation, and it was installed the day after purchase. Although the technician initially seemed to struggle with our narrow and unique kitchen layout, he kindly helped me think it through, which is another aspect I am satisfied with. With the birth of my child approaching, I felt burdened by dishwashing, so I reluctantly decided to buy at least a 6-person model, but I am much more satisfied than I expected. It is very easy to set up and is perfect for washing up leftovers from breakfast and dinner for a two-person household. My tendency to be bad at stacking might play a part, though. After using it for about three weeks, I find that since I tend to use a frying pan for meat or fried food for every meal and also use a pot occasionally, if I include the frying pan and pot, I think it can only handle about one meal. When I run it once a day, I exclude wooden tableware, frying pans, and pots. When I include pots and frying pans, I wash up a single meal. The button operation is also very simple. You just turn on the power (since there is a default mode) and press play. The default setting is 65 minutes, and it cleans everything squeaky clean. It worked perfectly on the frying pan used to grill LA galbi and even on the plate with the red grease left over from spicy chicken stew. You can also run additional rinse and wash functions, but I haven't used them yet. The UV sterilization mode and door opening function can be turned on/off, and since I think elderly people would find it easy to use, I am seriously considering buying one for my mom. However, for households of 3 or more, the 6-person size is too small, so I recommend the 12-14 person size. I recommend it for families of 1-2 people plus a baby, homes that cannot be built-in, or homes that do not require drilling holes. Regarding high-temperature drying, it is initially confusing because there is no separate drying function. If you pre-wash with water just once before putting them in, it cleans thoroughly, removing even grease stains, leaving both the inside and outside squeaky clean. However, some water does pool in the concave areas on the back of dishes where they are turned upside down. But since there is an automatic door opening function, if you run it after dinner and check the next morning, there are usually only a drop or two of water remaining in the concave areas on the back. We actually dislike even that, so we take them out to the sink to dry completely once they are done, but it is not inconvenient at all; in fact, I feel good about the squeaky-clean dishes! For reference, in our house, we cannot fully utilize the advantages of the L-shape and it only opens about 45 degrees because it gets caught on the faucet, but we are still satisfied with it. You just need to stack the first layer first, then assemble and fill the second layer. It might look a bit inconvenient to others, but the cleaning power and convenience are so satisfying that I hope those who need this for a kitchen with a unique layout like ours will take it into consideration when purchasing. If you have a larger kitchen, it unfolds completely into a straight L shape, making it much easier to use, so I recommend it. For reference, since ours is right next to the sink, we didn't need to drill a separate hole; we just ran the drain pipe directly to the sink and installed the water supply along the side wall, so we are satisfied with the appearance as well. Since Coupang handles after-sales service, I plan to use it comfortably. Above all, the price is half that of other brands, so I am very satisfied with it considering the cost!
